A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LongFinanceQA, PAI, and LongPAI research. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original PAI and LongPAI evaluations on Loong and ∞Bench, ablations, efficiency measurements, and appendix case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains original model evaluations and analyses, reports revised LongPAI results, and adds human evaluation of LongFinanceQA and additional inference-framework comparisons.

M1.justification: The property extraction, property-based retrieval, and summarization stages remain unchanged, as do LongPAI's context extension and supervised CoT objective. Standardizing PAI's name from Property-driven or Preference to Property-based does not alter its procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same bilingual LongFinanceQA collection, SlimPajama pretraining data, Loong tasks and domains, and ∞Bench English/Chinese QA coverage. The new human assessment samples existing LongFinanceQA questions without introducing a new domain or task scenario.

E2.justification: The inference-framework comparison expands from PAI− and RAG in v1 Table 5 to include Self-Ask and Self-Route in v2 Table 6. This substantially broadens comparison against reasoning-based retrieval approaches; the existing main and appendix LLM comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a human-evaluation protocol using 200 randomly selected questions, 10 volunteers, and 1–5 correctness ratings for answers and intermediate reasoning. Section 4.1 also changes the reported constant learning rate from 2e-6 to 1e-5, without explaining whether this reflects rerunning experiments or correcting documentation.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct human validation of synthetic answers and reasoning trajectories, substantially extending the data-quality analysis that v1 based on PAI's Loong performance. The existing CoT and property-extraction ablations, token-efficiency analysis, and two appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Table 2 introduces averaged human ratings with ± quantities, including an overall 4.29 ± 0.19; v1 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. The PDF does not define these quantities as standard deviations, standard errors, or confidence intervals, and adds no model-run or seed reporting.

E6.justification: LongPAI's financial overall AS/PR changes from 70.54/0.52 to 73.94/0.58, with revised task-level, ablation, and appendix entries. ∞Bench English/Chinese F1 changes from 32.46/32.38 to 32.65/32.88, and human ratings plus Self-Ask/Self-Route results are added. Because the reported learning rate changes, these are revised results rather than a controlled same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same conditional-probability formulation, reasoning/answer factorization, and training objective. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs beyond this existing mathematical formulation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction increase the claimed financial-subset improvement from 24.6% to 28.0%. The principal contributions—LongFinanceQA, the PAI framework, and supervised CoT for long-context understanding—retain their original scope.

C2.justification: v2 attributes gains primarily to high-quality synthesized data and adds a query-drift rationale for structured properties. It also identifies supervised-fine-tuning overfitting as a generalization concern and discusses possible regularization or reinforcement-learning remedies; broader generalization uncertainty and prompt dependence were already acknowledged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project homepage and revises the documented learning rate. Hardware, training duration, batch size, context-extension details, and appendix prompt specifications are largely retained. The supplied PDFs do not establish a new code or data release.

R1.justification: A new Agentic RAG discussion positions PAI as a hybrid of predefined and agentic reasoning, distinguishing structured properties and supervised transfer from prior approaches. References to Self-Ask, Self-Route, RAPTOR, ReAct, function calling, and an agentic-RAG survey substantially expand this positioning; additional citations support the expanded limitations.

P1.justification: v2 standardizes PAI terminology, makes localized language corrections, adds related-work and human-evaluation paragraphs, and expands the limitations. The main narrative and section structure, including Appendix A.1–A.6, remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the human-evaluation table, expands the inference comparison by two rows, and corrects the ablation caption's baseline name. Existing figures are retained with resizing, relocation, and renumbering; appendix figures move onto separate pages, and the full-results table caption moves above the table.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's indirect data-quality argument, the human audit supplies direct supporting evidence, while Self-Ask/Self-Route comparisons and expanded related work strengthen assessment against relevant approaches. These gains are limited: the human-rating ± statistic is undefined, and those ratings do not establish v2's stronger causal attribution of training gains to data quality.
